$comment: Single source of truth for the Helios Energy fiction. Never edit generated files by hand: run 'node scripts/build/universe.mjs' instead.

company.name: Helios Energy
company.pitch: Helios Energy installs residential solar panels in southern Europe. Sales runs on Salesforce, and the delivery crews track every installation in a custom app called Helios Delivery.

objects.label: Panel Batch
objects.role: child of Installation, one per pallet of panels delivered

permissionSets.label: Helios Delivery Crew
permissionSets.role: field crews: read installations, edit their own

permissionSets.label: Helios Delivery Manager
permissionSets.role: planners: full access plus the scheduler

cast.name: Sofia Marchetti
cast.role: Release manager. Left the company between Level 2 and Level 3, which is why the pipeline is yours now.

cast.name: Marco Bianchi
cast.role: Senior contributor. Merges before you do, on the files you touched.

cast.name: Amina Diallo
cast.role: Contributor, works on the quoting side of the app.

cast.name: You
cast.role: New joiner in Level 1, trusted contributor in Level 2, release manager in Level 3.

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Show the crew how many panels a job needs
userStories.story: As a delivery crew member, I want to see the number of panels required on the installation record, so that I load the right quantity on the van.
acceptance: A Panels Required field exists on Installation
It is visible to the crew permission set
Planners can fill it in
It appears on the Installation record page

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Let the crew leave notes on an installation
userStories.story: As a delivery crew member, I want a free text notes field and a list view of the installations still open, so that I hand over cleanly to the next shift.
acceptance: A Crew Notes field exists on Installation
An Open Installations list view exists, for every user
The crew permission set grants the field

userStories.author: amina
userStories.title: Record who signed an installation off
userStories.story: As a delivery manager, I want the name of whoever signed the installation off, so that I can call them when the customer rings back.
acceptance: The field is on the layout
Managers can read and write it

userStories.author: marco
userStories.title: Cap the crew size a planner can assign
userStories.story: As a planner, I want the assignment flow to refuse a crew larger than the installation allows, so that we stop over-staffing small jobs.
acceptance: Installation_Assign_Crew checks the cap
Planners can override it

userStories.author: amina
userStories.title: Generate a quote PDF from an opportunity
userStories.story: As a sales rep, I want a button that generates the quote PDF, so that I stop rebuilding it in a spreadsheet.
acceptance: The permission is granted to managers

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: The pipeline reaches production
userStories.story: As the release manager, I want preprod and main in the pipeline, with their orgs and their merge path, so that every release reaches production the same way.
acceptance: preprod and main are major branches with their own org
integration merges into uat, uat into preprod, preprod into main
Contributors can target preprod for a hotfix

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: CI authentication with JWT
userStories.story: As the release manager, I want every CI job to log in with a certificate through an External Client App, so that no pipeline depends on one person's refresh token.
acceptance: integration, uat, preprod and main each have an encrypted key file and two secrets
No SFDX_AUTH_URL secret is left in the repository
The integration check job logs in with JWT

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Total Capacity back on the Installation layout
userStories.story: As a planner, I want to see the installed capacity on an installation again, so that I stop opening the report to find it.
acceptance: Total Capacity (kW) is on the Installation layout, beside the crew capacity cap

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Release notes of the 2026-09 promotion
userStories.story: As the release manager, I want the notes of each promotion in the repository, so that the business reads what changed without asking.
acceptance: The notes open with what the release is for
The manual steps name who does them

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Project documentation
userStories.story: As the release manager, I want the project documented from its sources, so that an admin can read what an object or a flow does without opening Setup.
acceptance: The generated pages are in docs/ on integration
The Installation page says what an installation is

userStories.author: marco
userStories.title: Refactor InstallationScheduler
userStories.story: As a developer, I want the scheduler split into testable methods, so that we stop being afraid of it.
acceptance: Behaviour unchanged
Coverage above the threshold

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Warn the planner when a crew is too small
userStories.story: As a planner, I want a warning on the installation when the assigned crew is smaller than the job needs, so that I fix it before the van leaves.
acceptance: The flow reads Crew Size
A warning is shown
userStories.seededFailure: The Crew Size field is excluded by an over-eager .forceignore entry, so the flow deploys against a field that is not in the package

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Crew size becomes mandatory
userStories.story: As a planner, I want Crew Size to be mandatory on every installation, so that no job is scheduled without a crew.
acceptance: Crew Size is required
Existing records are backfilled with the default of 2
userStories.seededFailure: The permission sets still grant field level security on the field, which a required field cannot have, so the deployment fails on them. Once that is fixed the deployment goes green and silently makes the 30 installations with no crew size unsaveable, because Salesforce enforces a required field on save rather than on the data already there

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Crew capacity reference data and nightly recalculation
userStories.story: As a planner, I want capacity rules per crew type and a nightly job that recalculates them, so that the planning board is right every morning and I get a summary of it in my inbox.
acceptance: 12 Crew Capacity records exist in every org
The batch is scheduled nightly
The planner receives the morning summary email
userStories.seededFailure: The feature is silently inert after deployment because the reference records and the schedule exist in no org

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Check several installations against panel availability at once
userStories.story: As a planner, I want to check a list of installations against panel availability in one go, so that I can fill a week of planning without opening every record.
acceptance: InstallationScheduler returns the installations that can take a crew on a given day
Coverage stays above the threshold
userStories.seededFailure: The obvious implementation queries inside its loop, which PMD warns about, and the new branch has no test, which drops coverage below the threshold and blocks the deployment

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Crews can read the panel batch cost
userStories.story: As a delivery crew member, I want to see the cost of the batch I am installing, so that I report damage with the right value.
acceptance: The crew can read Panel Batch Cost
userStories.seededFailure: The permission was granted on a Profile that overwrite management protects, so the deployment is green and the permission is missing

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Flat roofs need a crew of at least three
userStories.story: As a planner, I want the assignment flow to put at least three people on a flat roof, so that the ballast is carried safely.
acceptance: Installation_Assign_Crew raises the crew on flat roofs
Marco crew cap from US-018 still wins when the two disagree
userStories.seededFailure: Marco US-018 merged first and touched the same flow and the same permission set

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Tidy the Installation layout
userStories.story: As a planner, I want Crew Size above Install Date on the installation layout, so that I see the staffing before the date.
acceptance: Crew Size sits above Install Date on the Installation layout
userStories.seededFailure: None. The lab is about publishing far too much and recovering from it

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Installation handover checklist
userStories.story: As a planner, I want a handover checklist on the installation with its reference items, so that a job is only closed when the checklist is complete.
acceptance: A Handover_Item__c object exists
10 reference checklist items are loaded in every org
The close flow blocks on an incomplete checklist
userStories.seededFailure: Combines the dependency error of US-021, the data action of US-026 and a conflict with a teammate branch

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Cancelled installations can no longer be back-dated
userStories.story: As a planner, I want to back-date an installation I cancel to the day it was called off, so that the week can be closed.
acceptance: Cancelled installations are exempt from the date rule, like completed ones
The rule still refuses to move a planned installation into the past
userStories.seededFailure: The date validation rule exempts Completed installations and not Cancelled ones, so every back-dated cancellation is refused

userStories.author: you
userStories.title: Needs Reinspection status, added in production by an admin
userStories.story: As the release manager, I want the status an admin added in production to be in the repository, so that the next release does not take it away from the planners.
acceptance: Needs Reinspection is a value of Installation__c.Status__c on integration
Nothing else from production came with it

labs.title: Install VS Code, Git and sfdx-hardis
labs.description: Install Git, Node.js, VS Code and the sfdx-hardis extension, then let its Setup panel install the Salesforce CLI and plugins without typing a command.

labs.title: Create your Dev Hub, scratch orgs and CI/CD pipeline
labs.description: Sign up for one free Salesforce Developer Edition org, then let one click create a Dev Hub, three scratch orgs, your GitHub fork and its CI/CD pipeline.

labs.title: Start a User Story on its own Git branch
labs.description: Take your first ticket from the backlog and create its Git branch and development org with the New User Story button of the sfdx-hardis VS Code extension.

labs.title: Build a custom field in your Salesforce org
labs.description: Create a custom field, grant it through a permission set and add it to the page layout in Salesforce Setup, in your own development scratch org.

labs.title: Retrieve, commit and publish your Salesforce changes
labs.description: Bring your org changes into Git with the sfdx-hardis Metadata Retriever, stage only the files of your story, commit, and publish your branch.

labs.title: Open a Pull Request, pass the deployment check, merge
labs.description: Open a GitHub Pull Request, read the sfdx-hardis deployment check and its comment, merge, and watch CI/CD deploy your change to the integration org.

labs.title: Capstone: deliver a User Story on your own
labs.description: Deliver a Salesforce User Story end to end with no step-by-step: branch, build, retrieve, commit, Pull Request and deployment with sfdx-hardis.

labs.title: Backpromote: catch your org up with the team
labs.description: Your development org is behind integration. Bring in the stories your teammates merged with the sfdx-hardis Backpromote panel, keeping your own work.

labs.title: Fix a deployment error caused by a missing dependency
labs.description: A Pull Request deployment check fails. Read the Salesforce error properly and find the component a .forceignore entry silently left out.

labs.title: Fix broken records with an Apex deployment action
labs.description: Making a field required deploys green and breaks existing records. Fix it with a pre-deployment Apex script declared as an sfdx-hardis deployment action.

labs.title: Ship reference data and a batch with deployment actions
labs.description: A green deployment is not a working feature. Ship reference data, a scheduled Apex batch and a manual step as sfdx-hardis deployment actions.

labs.title: Pass the code quality gate and Apex test coverage
labs.description: Fix a PMD warning and the Apex code coverage that block your Pull Request, and run the same checks from VS Code before you push.

labs.title: Permission sets, profiles and why a grant disappears
labs.description: A permission granted on a Profile vanishes after a green deployment. Learn how sfdx-hardis cleans profiles, and grant access with a permission set.

labs.title: Resolve a Git merge conflict with a teammate
labs.description: A teammate merged first on the same flow and permission set. Resolve both Git conflicts in VS Code without losing anybody's work.

labs.title: Recover from committing the wrong metadata
labs.description: You published far more than your story. See what it does to a Pull Request, and recover with the two sfdx-hardis ways out.

labs.title: Capstone: deliver a User Story that has it all
labs.description: Deliver one Salesforce User Story with a dependency to check, a data deployment action and a teammate on the same permission set, with no step-by-step.

labs.title: Configure the CI/CD pipeline up to production
labs.description: Turn a two-stage Salesforce pipeline into four stages up to production: major branches, their orgs and merge targets in sfdx-hardis Pipeline Settings.

labs.title: Set up CI authentication with JWT for four orgs
labs.description: Replace auth URL secrets with JWT authentication through an External Client App for every major org, configured by sfdx-hardis, and prove it works.

labs.title: Review and merge a contributor Pull Request
labs.description: Review a teammate's Salesforce Pull Request as a release manager: find what the deployment check missed, request a change, and merge.

labs.title: Deploy to integration and read the deployment log
labs.description: Read an sfdx-hardis deployment log properly, and understand why what was deployed to the integration org is smaller than what changed.

labs.title: Three Pull Requests collide: choose the merge order
labs.description: Decide the order three Pull Requests are merged in when two change the same file and one fails its check, as a Salesforce release manager.

labs.title: Promote to UAT and write the release notes
labs.description: Promote integration to UAT, read the deployment actions the promotion carries, and generate release notes the business can read, with sfdx-hardis.

labs.title: Release to production and read your DORA metrics
labs.description: Release through preprod to your production org, verify it, then measure deployment frequency, lead time and failure rate with a DORA report.

labs.title: Production is broken: hotfix and retrofit
labs.description: Ship a Salesforce hotfix from preprod to production without breaking the pipeline, then bring a change an admin made in production back into Git.

labs.title: Monitor your production org
labs.description: Set up nightly sfdx-hardis monitoring on your Salesforce production org, read its first report, and decide which alerts are worth receiving.

labs.title: Generate the Salesforce project documentation
labs.description: Generate readable documentation of an undocumented Salesforce org with sfdx-hardis: objects, flows, Apex and permissions, from the sources in Git.

labs.title: Capstone: run a weekly release cycle
labs.description: Run a full week as a Salesforce release manager with no step-by-step: review, integrate, promote to UAT, release to production and measure.
